paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: loving your neighbor is something you DO, not something you know. The expert in the law had the right answer ready. He quoted "Love your neighbor as yourself." Jesus told him, "Do this and you will live" (Luke 10:27-28).

Then the expert wanted to justify himself and asked, "And who is my neighbor?" (Luke 10:29). Jesus answered with a story, and then He turned the question around. He didn't ask who deserves the expert's love. He asked, "Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?" (Luke 10:36). The Samaritan saw the hurt man, had compassion, and gave his time, his own animal and his money (Luke 10:33-35).

So here's what I take from it. Being a neighbor means showing mercy to whoever is in front of you, and I'd bet that's not always the person you'd pick. The expert said, "The one who showed him mercy," and Jesus told him, "Go and do likewise" (Luke 10:37). I know a little about being left in a dark place, friend, so I think mercy that stops and acts is a beautiful thing, and it's an invitation for you, too.
